about: Known gaps: brochure cost terms the app's estimate does not include (affects_cost true), and brochure contradictions (kind 'conflict': affects_cost false keeps one about a figure the estimate does not use as data only; affects_cost true marks the total estimated and shows the text, which then says the brochure contradicts itself, what each statement is and which one the estimate uses), and plans whose brochure does not state a per-person out-of-pocket limit (kind 'cap_not_stated': affects_cost false, enrollments self_plus_one and family; the estimate caps each person at the plan's own Self Only maximum, the app's stated assumption, and 'See the math' shows the text for those enrollments without changing the total or marking it estimated; the text must name that Self Only maximum). enrollments (optional): the enrollments the entry applies to, all when absent. applies_when (optional): the care that can trigger a cost gap (hospital: a hospital stay or a maternity line; outpatient_surgery; imaging: MRI/CT; brand_drugs: a drug above the generic tier; medical_care: any care other than pharmacy fills; any_care: any care at all, medications included); the note and the 'estimated' mark then appear only when someone's year includes it, every year when absent. pipeline/build_data.py attaches each entry to data/benefits.json under benefits[year][plan_code]['known_gaps'] and checks that each quote occurs on the named brochure page (pipeline/raw/brochures_txt/<year>/<brochure>.txt, whitespace-insensitive). amounts: {self, self_plus_one, family} or null where the brochure gives no amounts by enrollment. text is the sentence shown to users in 'See the math', after 'Not included in this estimate:' for a cost term and on its own for a conflict.

gaps.text: a $500 calendar-year deductible that applies to inpatient and outpatient hospital services and MRI/CT scans. The brochure does not say whether it is per person or per family, so the estimate may be low by $500 for each person or each family.
gaps.quote: The calendar year deductible is $500, which applies to inpatient and outpatient hospital services
gaps.reason: OPM's spreadsheet and the app carry no deductible. The brochure (p25, p26) has a $500 deductible limited to hospital services and MRI/CT; it gives no amounts per enrollment type and does not say per person or per family. Not modeled.

gaps.text: a hospital facility deductible on inpatient and outpatient hospital charges, including lab tests, X-rays and other diagnostic services and clinic visits at an outpatient hospital: $250 for Self Only, $500 for Self Plus One and for Self and Family. The estimate may be low by up to that amount.
gaps.quote: separate in-network and out-of-network $250 inpatient and outpatient hospital facility deductible
gaps.reason: The app's deductible is $0 / $0 / $0. The brochure has a hospital-facility-only deductible, in-network and out-of-network. Section 5(c) (p74-75) applies it to outpatient hospital non-surgical and clinic visits ("deductible, then $100 copay") and to diagnostic services received at an outpatient hospital ("the deductible applies in addition to the copay"). The app does not know where care is received, so any medical care in the year (not pharmacy fills) can trigger it. Not modeled.

gaps.text: The brochure contradicts itself about the Self Plus One and Self and Family deductible: it says the deductible is $2,000 per person, met for the family once two members each meet theirs (pages 25 and 102), but also that one or more family members can meet the $4,000 family deductible (page 104); the estimate uses the shared $4,000 deductible, so it may be too high by up to $2,000.
gaps.quote: The deductible is $2,000 per person ($4,000 per Self Plus One enrollment
gaps.reason: TakeCare HDHP. Section 4 (p25) and Section 5 (p102, p171) say the Self and Family deductible is met when at least two covered family members have met their individual deductible; p104 and the other Section 5 subsections (p117, p126, p129, p132, p135) say it can be satisfied by one or more family members. The brochure states no individual threshold for one person. The app keeps the shared $4,000 deductible (aggregate).

gaps.text: The brochure contradicts itself about the Self Plus One and Self and Family deductible: Sections 4 and 5 give it as $3,500 per family unit, but the Summary (page 172) gives $1,650 per person, and a line later $1,750 per person, up to $3,500 for the family; the estimate uses the shared $3,500 deductible, so for one person it may be too high by up to $1,850.
gaps.quote: Self Plus One or Self and Family enrollment is $3,500 per family unit
gaps.reason: Kaiser Permanente Washington Options Federal HDHP. Section 4 (p26), the changes page (p18) and Section 5 (p100, p101, p117 and others) say $3,500 per family unit. The Summary (p172) says "$1,650 per person for Self Plus One or Self and Family enrollment" not to exceed $3,500, and one line later "$1,750 per person Self Plus One or Self and Family". The app keeps the shared $3,500 deductible (aggregate).

Probably a form-template leftover. Section 7 (p74) says "deductibles and maximum allowances apply separately to each person" (a record-keeping instruction). The separate pharmacy maximum ($4,600 Self Only) is not checked here.

gaps.reason: UPMC HDHP. Section 4 (p30) prints the same "Self Plus One $12,000 per person" line for the Standard Option, whose own example says each enrollee's maximum is $6,000, so the wording is a template leftover. The HDHP pages (p92, p104) say the family maximum "must be met by one or more members", which leans toward one family limit but does not say so.

gaps.text: The brochure says the plan’s $2,400 Personal Care Account is used first; after that, once one person meets a $1,000 net deductible coverage begins for that person, and once the other covered members meet an additional $1,000 it begins for them, so the family’s net deductible is $2,000 in all. The estimate instead gives each person a $2,200 deductible (up to $4,400 for the family) and subtracts the account money from the total. For one person with a chronic condition it may be about $1,000 too low; in other years it can be too high or too low.
gaps.quote: once one individual meets the Self Only Net Deductible of $1,000
gaps.reason: APWU Consumer Driven Option. Section 4 (p28): the plan deductible ($2,200 / $4,400 / $4,400) is reduced by the Personal Care Account ($1,200 / $2,400 / $2,400) used first, and the Net Deductible is $1,000 / $2,000 / $2,000; for Self Plus One and Self and Family one individual meets the $1,000 net deductible, the others the additional $1,000. The app (OPM's spreadsheet figures) gives each person the $2,200 Self Only deductible within $4,400 and subtracts the account money after (HRA offset). Measured with this tool's scenarios (2027, active): one person, chronic condition, Self Plus One or Family: the app is $1,020 lower than the brochure order; two people, typical year: the app is $615 higher; worst case: $0 or $2,400 lower depending on whether account payments count toward the out-of-pocket limit, which the brochure does not say (p31 says the limit applies once you have exceeded your account and met your deductible). Drugs count: p89 says prescription costs are paid from the PCA and then the net deductible during the deductible phase, so any care, medications included, can trigger the difference. Not modeled; Self Only matches the brochure order except for that out-of-pocket question.

gaps.text: The brochure says the plan’s Medical Fund ($900 for Self Only, $1,800 for Self Plus One or Self and Family) is used first, and only then does the whole deductible apply ($2,000 for Self Only, $4,000 for Self Plus One or Self and Family; under those two, once one person meets the $2,000 Self Only deductible coverage begins for that person); the fund does not reduce the deductible or the out-of-pocket maximum. The estimate instead lets the fund pay toward the deductible (it subtracts the fund money from what the care costs you), so it leaves out the deductible paid after the fund is used up and may be too low, by up to the fund amount.
gaps.quote: Once you have exhausted your medical fund, the annual deductible of $2,000
gaps.reason: Aetna Direct Plan. Brochure 73-828 p16-17: the Medical Fund ($900 / $1,800 / $1,800) is used first, then the deductible ($2,000 / $4,000 / $4,000) must be met; once one individual meets the $2,000 Self Only deductible coverage begins for that individual. p115 and p117: the Medical Fund does not reduce the deductible or the out-of-pocket maximum. p161: prescriptions too are paid after the fund is exhausted and the deductible satisfied, so any care, medications included, can trigger the difference. The app gives each person the $2,000 deductible (family $4,000) and subtracts the fund money afterwards (HRA offset, capped at expected costs), which lets the fund pay the deductible. Measured with this tool's scenarios (2027, active, one person; brochure order computed by giving that person a deductible and out-of-pocket maximum raised by the fund, then subtracting the fund; the app's own prices for the care): Self Plus One or Family: healthy and typical $0, chronic condition the app is $1,440 lower, worst case $1,800 lower. Self Only has the same order and the app is $720 (chronic condition) to $900 (worst) lower, so the entry applies to every enrollment (it changes no total, only the firmness and the note). Not modeled.
